counting_rule: One complete real development agent A/B comparison, explicit root-cause diagnosis, a justified product or evaluation-method correction, and a fresh matched A/B re-evaluation with independent quality grading. Direct MCP calls, unit tests, and repetitions without changes DO NOT count. Each accepted cycle must pass docs/benchmarks/audit_agent_effect_cycles.py against original Codex trace and graded results, including token/cache accounting, all 4 A/B trials, same model and seed per pair, successful model-initiated LSP use after correction, and full grade checks. Savings must not be claimed on cached-token cumulative counts alone.

found_problems: The grader counted tools.New(...) inside a quoted test fixture string as a real constructor invocation, producing false failures in both arms.
The connected agent unnecessarily requested preview_rename(preview_detail=full) with 5451 bytes while file-scope summary would suffice.
corrections: Replace the source-substring grader with a Go AST parser that inspects real imported selector call expressions, with regression checks for quoted examples.
Clarify LSP preview scope and the default summary in tool descriptions and agent work rules; allow full only when individual edit ranges are needed.
Replace fragile TYPE_DIAGNOSTICS_AGENTS string replacement, which broke after edits, with additive guidance.

after_rerun_summary.note: Separate stochastic A/B pairs. Tool-preview size difference is directly observed; time or token differences between runs are not causal proof of the repair.

cycles.evidence_note: Raw traces, results and corrected-grade JSON remain in isolated .scratch directories, not published because paths and assistant logs can contain sensitive context.

found_problems: Codex connected to full 22 tools but performed a trivial missing import manually; no model-initiated LSP usage in the first A/B pair.

Independent reproduction against typescript-language-server found get_code_actions intermittently fails with internal error Cannot read properties of null (reading filter). Root cause: Go nil slice serialized mandatory LSP CodeActionContext.diagnostics as JSON null, not an array.
The suggested TypeScript Update import action includes both an edit and a command; apply_code_action intentionally refuses partial application for safety.
corrections: Normalize required CodeActionContext.diagnostics to an empty JSON array when diagnostics have not yet been published; add a regression checking serialized JSON arrays.

Document a task-conditional code-actions policy equally for both A/B arms: consult LSP diagnostics and code-action suggestions when connected, but fall back to manual edit when execution of an LSP command would be required. Never force an LSP quota.

direct_reproduction.before: get_code_actions at the missing InvoiceSummary reference returned LSP INTERNAL_ERROR due to null diagnostics.
direct_reproduction.after: the same get_code_actions returned three suggestions, including a preferred Update import action, with valid diagnostics and no error.

after_rerun_summary.note: One stochastic pair, not a causal claim. The tool suggestions were informational; a manual import edit was still necessary because the action also required a command.

cycles.evidence_note: Detailed Codex events and direct TS tool responses are in local isolated .scratch logs. No model-completion API-only exercises counted.

found_problems: Even a task requiring complete structural Go interface implementation analysis used zero MCP calls with the generic agent policy. The connected arm spent 87.4s versus 33.0s for Codex-only despite equal quality. It relied on four textual shell commands.

The default agent instructions did not explain when find_implementations is materially more precise than matching similarly named methods. Direct gopls verification identified all three structural implementers of document.Notifier, including the test double.
corrections: Added independent, checkable semantic implementation task S01 requiring the three actual implementing types and exact source paths, with independent answer evidence in the A/B evaluator.

Added a semantic-implementations conditional agent policy to both A/B arms: when interface conformance matters and LSP is connected, consider find_implementations and verify completeness; without LSP, use ordinary source reasoning. No tool-use quotas or mandatory calls.

after_rerun_summary.note: This is one matched after pair, not proof of a population-wide advantage. Before and after were separate randomized model runs; never attribute the time difference between runs causally to prompt revision.

cycles.evidence_note: Codex turn traces and independently graded JSON files are held in local isolated .scratch directories.

found_problems: The connected agent requested inspect_symbol, preview_rename, and find_references for a read-only exhaustive impact file list. The preview was unrelated to the task and detailed source lines were unnecessary. The first MCP trial called 3 tools, consuming 6428 response bytes.

The independent exact-files answer oracle was present in the frozen Go repository copy (though recorded agent commands did not access the Python oracle); contaminating future blinded evaluations was possible.
corrections: Document direct find_references(path,symbol_path,relation_view=locations) when a declaration identity is already known. Distinguish read-only impact analysis from write-intent semantic rename in the shared agent policy.
Update the find_references MCP tool description: avoid preview_rename and inspect_symbol for known target identities; use locations for path-only questions.
Exclude docs/benchmarks entirely from the frozen Go source copy for both agent arms, protecting independent scoring keys and grading logic. Preserve original source and independent external grader.

after_rerun_summary.limitation: The connected agent still requested relation_view=lines rather than locations, so 4336 bytes of detailed references remain. Small one-pair result is not a statistically conclusive productivity effect.

cycles.evidence_note: Before raw model calls were audited to exclude oracle reading, but frozen oracle exposure is a methodological flaw and is disclosed. After fresh run has no grader assets in either model workspace. Baseline used gopls CLI, so comparison is native Codex capabilities vs MCP connector, not a proof of no language server without MCP.

found_problems: The connected agent wrongly guessed /Store/SyncBytes in Go although gopls identifies this pointer method as (*Store).SyncBytes, causing two failed MCP attempts.

The agent then requested get_document_symbols and both find_references and get_incoming_calls, even though one successful get_incoming_calls suffices to identify the four direct callers. Five tool attempts increased noncached input tokens from 7529 to 31658 (plus 320%).
corrections: Changed get_incoming_calls tool description to explicitly demonstrate Go pointer-method LSP symbol_path /(*Store).SyncBytes and discourage unverified /Store/SyncBytes guesses.

Added same-to-both-arms call-hierarchy work policy: use one get_incoming_calls call for known exact method identity, get_document_symbols only if unknown; avoid token-consuming redundant calls and artificial tool quotas.
Added a held-out S03 read-only task with four exact named caller path+function pairs and deterministic strict JSON independent grading.

after_rerun_summary.limitation: One matched after A/B pair, not a statistically significant general speed benefit. Noncached input tokens remained ~9.8% higher on MCP arm.

cycles.evidence_note: Direct gopls call-hierarchy oracle returned four named callers and complete=true; both after agent answers exactly match the held-out expected object list. Trace kept isolated.

found_problems: For the 15 distinct outgoing callees of (*Engine).Relationship, the connected model guessed /Engine/Relationship and received a failed MCP call.

It then requested get_document_symbols(detail=full), returning 5500 bytes, and used the discovered symbol ID to get the 5691-byte outgoing relation. This extra lookup and retry made the connected agent 42.5s vs the baseline 26.3s and used 21701 vs 19680 noncached input tokens.
corrections: Added an actual Go outgoing semantic call graph S04 task with an independent exact oracle containing 15 name/path pairs, holding oracle files outside both workspaces.
Updated the get_outgoing_calls tool discovery text to show direct Go pointer receiver method syntax /(*Engine).Relationship, and discourage incorrect /Engine/Relationship.
Added a conditional outbound call hierarchy policy, identical between arms, emphasizing one get_outgoing_calls request for a known method and no redundant source rereads; no mandatory LSP calls.

after_rerun_summary.note: One-pair observed result: speed improved ~33.5%, noncached tokens increased ~114%, and both answered all 15 exact name/path pairs. Not a universal statistically significant result.

cycles.evidence_note: Before and after are independent A/B pairs. Direct prior gopls outgoingCalls returned complete=true and 15 distinct callees. Raw logs kept local.

found_problems: Call hierarchy tools returned full LSP range and identity objects (5691 bytes for 15 callees) even when the task requested only exact callee names and file paths; this wastes context on irrelevant details.

Previous reports equated similar total-token counts with similar monetary cost. The cached/noncached split has different cost weights and model-call counts, so total input alone is not a reliable cost proxy.
corrections: Added optional hierarchy_view=name_path to incoming/outgoing calls; preserve full result by default, retain completeness/truncation metadata and reject entries whose declaration path cannot be established.
Changed the task-conditional same-to-both-arms agent instruction to prefer hierarchy_view=name_path for name/file-only call-graph queries. No forced MCP calls.

Added an independent agent-level ledger auditor that verifies trace token usage, model requests, exact A/B seed hashes, actual MCP invocations, completion and quality, and calculates input cost scenarios without inventing dollar pricing.

direct_reproduction.task: get_outgoing_calls on /(*Engine).Relationship, same live gopls and workspace

after_rerun_summary.note: One stochastic post-correction A/B pair; tool-payload reduction is directly measured against identical LSP data. Do not infer equal billing cost from total tokens, nor attribute all timing changes to the new view.

cycles.evidence_note: Raw traces preserved in isolated .scratch; independently inspected by docs/benchmarks/audit_agent_effect_cycles.py.

found_problems: The pre-change connected Codex agent requested find_references relation_view=locations for a file-only impact task; the MCP response was 5178 bytes of repeated ranges and file names for 16 distinct files.
A per-hit result limit can silently hide distinct impacted files when a single file has many reference hits. A file-only query must limit unique paths rather than raw LSP hits.
corrections: Implement reference_view=files for find_references with sorted unique paths, a file-based limit, complete/truncated metadata, and the original reference_count and filter metadata.
Expose a restricted file-view MCP schema and task-conditional agent instructions for exact path-only impact analysis; preserve position/source variants.
Add pure regression cases for unique file limits, real gopls reference resolution and test filtering, MCP argument validation, and profile catalog bounds. Verify race-enabled Go tests and go vet.

direct_reproduction.note: First tool response reduction is directly observed. The after agent made an unnecessary second lines call, so total MCP payload and noncached model cost do not improve in the same proportion.

after_rerun_summary.note: Both answers passed independent exact 16-file grading; the model used the new file view, but also unnecessarily requested line context. One stochastic pair is not proof of a causal speed improvement. Fresh input increased relative to baseline.

cycles.evidence_note: All four Codex results, original event traces, manifests, independent exact file-list grades and token usage are retained under the named isolated .scratch directories. Raw traces are not published.

uncounted_evaluations.why_not_counted: Not a distinct corrected and revalidated causal agent-effect cycle; it checks a configuration hypothesis across separate snapshots. No proven monetary savings.

uncounted_evaluations.reason: Both A/B arms failed before producing model tokens or a usable answer; no MCP use; independent answer-evidence grade failed. Invalid baseline, no causal improvement or after comparison; do not count.
